corrections.text: The article's Overview section attributes to The Stack the claim that virtual machines 'kept running during the incident but in many cases became unreachable.' The Stack's article does not contain this specific claim in its publicly accessible text. The fact itself is accurate and is independently confirmed by Techzine, which reported that 'virtual machines continued running during the outage but became largely inaccessible,' and is consistent with Google's own incident report and SDxCentral's reporting that VMs were 'effectively isolated.'

The article quotes Neil Shah of Counterpoint Research as saying, in quotation marks, that the disruption stemmed from 'a routine internal network update or configuration tweak' that 'introduced routing failure across multiple zones.' In the cited Network World article, this wording is the reporter's paraphrased description of Shah's comments, not text presented in quotation marks as Shah's own words. Only a separate sentence beginning 'While most of the physical nodes...' is an actual direct quotation from Shah in the source.
